questions.q:
Name the energy store that is increased in each of the following.
(a) A rubber band is stretched. [1]
(b) A plant makes glucose by photosynthesis. [1]
(c) Water in a kettle is heated. [1]
ms: (c) internal (thermal) (allow kinetic energy of particles; not 'heat')
questions.model:
(a) Elastic (strain) energy.
(b) Chemical energy.
(c) Internal (thermal) energy.
questions.tip: Use the syllabus names of stores; 'heat energy' is not accepted.

questions.q: Define power and state its unit.
ms: work done per unit time / energy transferred per unit time (allow P = W ÷ t or ΔE ÷ t with symbols explained)
questions.model: Power is the work done (or energy transferred) per unit time. Its unit is the watt (W), equal to 1 J/s.

questions.q:
A student of mass 55 kg runs up a flight of stairs. The vertical height of the stairs is 3.0 m and she takes 4.2 s. g = 9.8 N/kg.
(a) Calculate the gravitational potential energy she gains. [2]
(b) Calculate the useful power she develops. [2]
questions.tip: Use the VERTICAL height, not the length along the stairs.

questions.q:
(a) Describe how a gas-fired power station produces electrical energy. In your answer refer to the boiler, turbine and generator. [3]
(b) Biofuels and fossil fuels can both be burned in power stations. State one advantage and one disadvantage of using biofuels instead of fossil fuels. [2]
ms: (a) gas burned (chemical energy) to heat water in the boiler, producing (high-pressure) steam
(a) turbine turns the generator, which produces electricity (electrical energy)
(b) advantage: renewable / can be regrown / CO₂ absorbed by crops as they grow (so less overall effect on climate)
(b) disadvantage: needs large areas of land (could grow food / destroys habitats) / still releases CO₂ (and pollutants) when burned
questions.model:
(a) The gas is burned and the energy released heats water in the boiler, turning it into high-pressure steam. The steam drives the turbine round, and the turbine turns the generator, which produces electricity.
(b) Advantage: biofuels are renewable because the crops can be regrown (and they absorb carbon dioxide as they grow).
Disadvantage: growing them needs large areas of land that could otherwise grow food or support wildlife.
questions.tip: Give the sequence in order: fuel → boiler/steam → turbine → generator.

questions.q:
A trolley of mass 0.80 kg is released from rest at the top of a ramp. The top of the ramp is 0.45 m vertically above the bottom. The trolley travels 1.5 m along the ramp and reaches the bottom with a speed of 2.4 m/s. g = 9.8 N/kg.
(a) Calculate the gravitational potential energy lost by the trolley. [2]
(b) Calculate the kinetic energy of the trolley at the bottom of the ramp. [2]
(c) Calculate the efficiency of the transfer from gravitational potential energy to kinetic energy. [1]
(d) Calculate the average frictional force acting on the trolley along the ramp. [2]
ms: (d) C1: energy wasted = 3.528 − 2.304 = 1.22 J and W = Fd so F = 1.22 ÷ 1.5 (ecf)
questions.model:
(a) ΔEp = mgΔh = 0.80 × 9.8 × 0.45 = 3.53 J ≈ 3.5 J.
(b) Ek = ½mv² = ½ × 0.80 × 2.4² = 2.30 J.
(c) Efficiency = 2.30 ÷ 3.53 × 100% = 65%.
(d) Energy wasted doing work against friction = 3.53 − 2.30 = 1.22 J.
W = Fd, so F = 1.22 ÷ 1.5 = 0.82 N.
questions.tip: In (d) the friction acts along the slope, so use the 1.5 m slope length, not the 0.45 m height.

questions.q:
In a small hydroelectric power station, 50 kg of water passes through the turbine every second after falling through a vertical height of 120 m. The electrical power output of the generator is 45 kW. g = 9.8 N/kg.
(a) Calculate the gravitational potential energy lost by the water each second. [2]
(b) Calculate the efficiency of the power station. [2]
(c) State one advantage and one disadvantage of hydroelectric power compared with a coal-fired power station. [2]
ms: (b) C1: efficiency = useful power output ÷ total power input (× 100%) = 45 000 ÷ 58 800
(c) advantage: renewable / no CO₂ or polluting gases when generating / reliable, can be switched on quickly when demand rises
(c) disadvantage: flooding of valleys destroys habitats / homes / farmland; few suitable sites; high building cost
questions.model:
(a) ΔEp = mgΔh = 50 × 9.8 × 120 = 58 800 J each second (input power 58.8 kW).
(b) Efficiency = 45 000 ÷ 58 800 × 100% = 77%.
(c) Advantage: it is renewable and produces no carbon dioxide while generating. Disadvantage: building the dam floods a large area, destroying habitats and farmland.
questions.tip: Energy lost per second is a power: J/s = W. Keep both powers in the same unit before dividing.
